- **Animated Carousel**: Smooth left-to-right scrolling animation with 30-second cycle duration

- **Interactive Elements**: Hover effects that pause animation and provide visual feedback
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-optimized card sizes and spacing
- **Seamless Loop**: Infinite scroll effect for continuous display
- **Professional Styling**: Gradient overlays and modern card design

## 🔧 Technical Changes

### Component Updates
- Replaced `<details>` dropdown with horizontal scrolling carousel
- Added custom CSS animations using `@keyframes` and `animate-scroll` class
- Implemented hover pause functionality for better UX
- Enhanced responsive design with mobile-first approach

### Styling Improvements
- Added gradient overlays for smooth edge fading
- Implemented card hover effects with scale and lift animations
- Updated card dimensions for better mobile experience
- Enhanced typography hierarchy and spacing

### Animation System
- Custom scroll animation with 30-second duration
- Smooth infinite loop using duplicated items
- Hover pause functionality for user interaction

## 📱 Responsive Design

- **Mobile**: Compact cards (h-24 w-32) with optimized spacing
- **Desktop**: Full-size cards (w-48) with enhanced padding
- **Tablet**: Adaptive sizing between mobile and desktop
- **Overflow Handling**: Proper container constraints and smooth scrolling

author: senthilkumarkathirvel
body:
This commit introduces a dark mode and light mode toggling feature to the application.

- A button has been added to the `AppComponent` to allow users to switch between light and dark themes.
- The theme state is managed within the `AppComponent` and a `dark-mode` class is applied to the `body` element when dark mode is active.
- Global styles have been updated to use CSS variables for theming, with separate color palettes for light and dark modes.
- The component-specific styles have been updated to use the new theme variables.
- The implementation is server-side rendering (SSR) compatible by using `isPlatformBrowser` to ensure DOM manipulation only happens on the client-side.

This change modifies  the code generators to emit explicit property declarations and assignments instead.

```typescript
private bridge: IHttpApiBridge;
constructor(bridge: IHttpApiBridge) {
  this.bridge = bridge;
}
```

Changes:
- Modified generateNonThrowingService.ts and generateThrowingService.ts to use explicit property declarations
- Updated all test expectations using `RECREATE=true` flag
- Fixed hardcoded test assertions to expect new constructor format

This ensures generated TypeScript services are compatible with strip-only mode while maintaining identical runtime behavior.

```

supported in strip-only mode, causing runtime errors. This change modifies
```

author: idrokin117
body:
# Summary

Resolves #869

This fix ensures that when accessing properties on generic type parameters with union constraints (e.g., T: A | B), the type checker correctly resolves the property return type instead of treating it as the TypeVar itself.

## Explanation

To access TypeVar methods with union bounds, we must ensure that each union member type has the specified method. Currently, Pyrefly bound union types to self when accessing methods, rather than to concrete types. This fix should resolve that issue.

## Test Plan

- Added several test cases to ensure correctness of method calling on TypeVar with union bound and restrictions.

author: bugclerk
body:
## Problem

When truenas is virtualized using xen, disks can appear in the system as `xvdb` etc and in this case their disk identifier shows up as `''` and eventually we cannot have more then one disk in the disk table because we have a UNIQUE constraint on identifiers.

Why identifier shows up as `''` because when trying to gauge identifier, it gets available disks and if the disk in question is not found there, it skips it (it is not nice but we are going to redo this logic separately).

## Solution

Make sure the regex we have which covers the disks we support actually accounts for xen disks as well.

Original PR: https://github.com/truenas/middleware/pull/16960

author: bugclerk
body:
## Problem

When truenas is virtualized using xen, disks can appear in the system as `xvdb` etc and in this case their disk identifier shows up as `''` and eventually we cannot have more then one disk in the disk table because we have a UNIQUE constraint on identifiers.

Why identifier shows up as `''` because when trying to gauge identifier, it gets available disks and if the disk in question is not found there, it skips it (it is not nice but we are going to redo this logic separately).

## Solution

Make sure the regex we have which covers the disks we support actually accounts for xen disks as well.

Original PR: https://github.com/truenas/middleware/pull/16960

body:
# [BE4-03] Implement Retrospective Engine with KPI Storage & Rule-based Insight Generation

## 📋 Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive retrospective analysis engine that automatically generates insights and reports for completed campaigns. The system collects multi-platform KPI data, applies rule-based analysis, and generates actionable recommendations with approval workflows.

## 🎯 Features Implemented

### Core Models
- **`RetrospectiveTask`**: Main orchestration model managing the entire retrospective lifecycle
- **`CampaignKPI`**: Multi-platform KPI storage with automatic metric calculations (ROI, CTR, conversion rates)
- **`Insight`**: Rule-generated insights with analyst review workflow and confidence scoring
- **`InsightCategory`**: Categorization system for better insight organization

### Celery Task Engine
- **`generate_retrospective()`**: Main orchestration task with retry logic and error handling
- **`collect_platform_kpis()`**: Multi-platform data collection (Google Ads, Facebook, TikTok, Instagram)
- **`generate_insights()`**: Rule-based insight generation with configurable business logic
- **`create_retrospective_report()`**: PDF/PPT report generation with professional formatting
- **`schedule_retrospective_for_campaign()`**: Auto-scheduling triggered on campaign completion
- **`cleanup_failed_retrospectives()`**: Maintenance task for retry logic and cleanup

### Rule-Based Insight Engine
Implemented **6 intelligent business rules**:

1. **ROI Rule**: Detects poor performance (< 0.7 threshold) and excellent performance (> 2.0)
2. **CTR Rule**: Analyzes click-through rates and identifies creative optimization opportunities
3. **Conversion Rate Rule**: Identifies funnel optimization and landing page issues
4. **Cost Efficiency Rule**: Monitors CPC/CPA thresholds and suggests bid optimizations
5. **Platform Performance Rule**: Cross-platform performance comparison and budget reallocation
6. **Budget Allocation Rule**: Efficiency analysis and spend optimization recommendations

### Report Generation
- **PDF Reports**: Professional reports with campaign overview, KPI tables, and insights
- **PPT Reports**: PowerPoint generation support (optional feature)
- **File Storage**: Integrated with Django storage system for scalable file management
- **Report URLs**: Automatic storage and URL generation for easy access

## 🏗️ Technical Implementation

### Database Design
- **4 main models** with optimized relationships and database indexes
- **Foreign key constraints** with appropriate CASCADE/SET_NULL behavior
- **JSON fields** for flexible metadata storage (conditions, raw platform data)
- **Performance optimizations** with strategic database indexes on frequently queried fields

### Architecture Patterns
- **Service Layer**: Clean separation between business logic and data access
- **Rule Engine Pattern**: Extensible system for adding new insight generation rules
- **Mock Data Service**: Development-friendly mock data generators for all platforms
- **WebSocket Ready**: Notification service prepared for real-time UI updates

### Error Handling & Reliability
- **Retry Logic**: Celery tasks with exponential backoff and jitter
- **Transaction Safety**: Atomic operations for data consistency
- **Graceful Degradation**: System continues functioning when external services fail
- **Comprehensive Logging**: Detailed logging throughout all components

## 📊 Example Output

The system automatically generates actionable insights such as:

- **"Poor ROI Performance"** → "Google Ads ROI of 0.6 is below target. Review audience targeting and keywords."
- **"High Cost Per Acquisition"** → "Facebook CPA of $75 exceeds threshold. Optimize bidding strategies and audience segments."
- **"Platform Performance Imbalance"** → "TikTok underperforming (score: 45) vs Facebook (score: 78). Consider budget reallocation."
- **"Excellent Cost Efficiency"** → "Google Ads achieving $8 CPA. Consider scaling this campaign."

## 🧪 Testing

### Comprehensive Test Suite (27 tests)
- **Model Tests**: Full coverage of model behavior, relationships, and validations
- **Task Tests**: Celery task functionality, error handling, and retry logic
- **Rule Engine Tests**: Insight generation logic and business rule validation
- **Integration Tests**: End-to-end workflow testing

### Test Coverage
```bash
python manage.py test retrospective.tests.test_models  # ✅ 27/27 passing
python manage.py test retrospective.tests.test_tasks   # ✅ All task scenarios covered
```

## 🚀 API Endpoints

### REST API Structure
```
GET    /retrospective/api/retrospectives/           # List retrospective tasks
POST   /retrospective/api/retrospectives/           # Create new task
GET    /retrospective/api/retrospectives/{id}/      # Get specific task
PUT    /retrospective/api/retrospectives/{id}/      # Update task

GET    /retrospective/api/insights/                 # List insights
POST   /retrospective/api/insights/{id}/review/     # Review insight
GET    /retrospective/api/rules/                    # List available rules

GET    /retrospective/health/                       # Health check
```

## 🔧 Configuration

### Django Settings
```python
INSTALLED_APPS += ['retrospective']

# Optional configuration
RETROSPECTIVE_USE_MOCK_DATA = True          # Use mock data for development
RETROSPECTIVE_AUTO_GENERATE_REPORTS = True  # Auto-generate PDF reports
RETROSPECTIVE_DELAY_HOURS = 1               # Hours after campaign completion
RETROSPECTIVE_GENERATE_PPT = False          # Enable PowerPoint generation
```

### URL Configuration
```python
urlpatterns = [
    path('retrospective/', include('retrospective.urls')),
]
```

## 📦 Dependencies Added

New dependencies required:
```txt
reportlab==4.0.4       # PDF generation
python-pptx==0.6.21    # PowerPoint generation (optional)
faker==19.3.0          # Mock data generation for testing
```

## 🔄 Workflow

1. **Campaign Completion**: Signal triggers retrospective scheduling
2. **KPI Collection**: Automated collection from multiple platforms (mock data for now)
3. **Rule Analysis**: 6 business rules analyze performance and generate insights
4. **Report Generation**: Professional PDF reports created automatically
5. **Approval Workflow**: Data analysts review insights, team leads approve reports
6. **Notifications**: WebSocket-ready real-time updates (framework in place)

## 🔐 Security & Permissions

- **Authentication Required**: All API endpoints require user authentication
- **Role-Based Access**: Framework prepared for Data Analyst/Team Lead permissions
- **Data Validation**: Comprehensive input validation and sanitization
- **Safe Defaults**: Conservative thresholds and graceful error handling

## 🚧 Future Enhancements

Ready for implementation when needed:
- **Real Platform APIs**: Replace mock data with actual Google Ads, Facebook, TikTok APIs
- **WebSocket Integration**: Real-time UI updates during processing
- **Advanced Permissions**: Granular role-based access control
- **Custom Rules**: UI for creating custom business rules
- **Dashboard Integration**: Analytics dashboard with charts and visualizations

## 📋 Database Migrations

```bash
python manage.py makemigrations retrospective  # ✅ Created 0001_initial.py
python manage.py migrate                       # ✅ Applied successfully
```

## ✅ Testing Instructions

1. **Run Tests**:
   ```bash
   python manage.py test retrospective
   ```

2. **Create Test Data**:
   ```bash
   python manage.py shell
   >>> from retrospective.tasks import schedule_retrospective_for_campaign
   >>> schedule_retrospective_for_campaign('campaign-uuid-here')
   ```

3. **Check Admin Interface**:
   - Navigate to `/admin/retrospective/`
   - View retrospective tasks, KPIs, and insights

That's approximately 1.3 × 10⁴⁹ possible keys
Practically impossible to guess or brute force

author: fw-bot
body:
Ticket #4992568 highlighted a weird way of sending the industry from IAP to the Odoo client. Before this commit, we were sending the IAP psql id of the industry to the client. There, it would be use as is. It works because these industries haven't been changed in years and they're created in the same order.
However the ticket highlighted the fact that a user can edit/delete/create its own industries, therefore some ids that exist on IAP might not exist on the client's Odoo instance. This resulted in a traceback on the client's side.

With this commit, we now send the industry code (the ISIC: International Standard Industrial Classification) instead to the client. There it can correctly be mapped if it exists on the client's DB (e.g. not deleted)

body:
Other git plugins, such as LFS, are shipped as "git-foo" packages. A reasonable user might expect to be able to install the git obs plugin by installing a "git-obs" package, but this does not work currently.

With this patch, a user attempting to install "git-obs" will get the git obs plugin via osc.

body:
Fixes #6

## Phone Number Verification Login Feature

### Overview
This pull request implements an automatic login mechanism via phone number verification to improve user experience by:
- Allowing users to skip manual username/password entry
- Verifying user identity through phone number
- Providing a seamless authentication flow

### Key Changes
- Added `login_whatsapp_by_number()` function in `moses_api.py`
- Modified `process_bot_response()` in `app.py` to support phone number verification
- Implemented handling for single and multiple branch scenarios
- Created personalized greeting for verified users

### Implementation Details
- Phone number verification uses existing webservice endpoint
- Supports both single and multiple branch login scenarios
- Fallback to traditional username/password flow if verification fails
- Personalized greeting with client name when verification succeeds

### Verification Logic
- Calls `/LoginWhatsappByNumber` endpoint with user's phone number
- Positive response: Skip username/password, proceed to subject selection
- Negative response: Continue with traditional login flow

### Handling Multiple Branches
- Detects multiple branches in API response
- Defaults to first available branch
- Logs multiple branch scenarios for future enhancement

### User Experience Improvements
- Faster login process
- Personalized greeting
- Immediate access to service selection

### Notes
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing authentication flow
- Comprehensive logging for debugging
- Flexible implementation for future extensions

author: souvikmukherjee199
body:
This PR closes issue:
#260  

PR Title:
Sign-Up-Loader-Redirect-route fixed

**Description**
This PR introduces the following changes-> 
1.Replaced the HashRouter with BrowserRouter for better SEO and  routing.
2. The Profile component from now onwards uses useUser, SignOutButton  from '@clerk/clerk-react for rendering the dynamic user profile information instead of the  { useAuth } from './context/AuthContext';
3. The AuthProvider component has been removed from the App.jsx and now uses the ClerkProvider for globally managing auth states 
4. The signup page has been revamped with the redirect url to '/login' after Google OAuth signup. Hence after signing up with google, user will be automatically redirected to the signin page for signing in.
5. A loader has been used for the sign-in and signup page to make them visually engaging and help the user understand the time delay for the redirection after signup or sign-in.
6. The initial error has that was caused by the nested link tag in Hero section has been fixed by wrapping the Link tag in MotionLink tag.
7. A new field has "username" has been introduced under the signup form. From now on, new users have to put their username, email Id and Password inside the signup form for creating their new account and will be automatically be logged in with new Session being created . After they have signed up using these aforementioned fields, they can logout and login again using the emailId and Password only.
8. A separate component for sso-callback has been created under the Auth directory for future references for further backend improvent in future along with "/verify" redirect route inclusion inside signup.jsx component for verification of email during signup process that can be worked on in future.
9. React-hot-toast has been used and staged for further development for custom sign-up and sign-in success messages in future.

**Demonstration_for_reviewers**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/979f3696-0481-48d3-9afb-d4264b9a7cbb


The above video effectively helps to understand the following:
1. How to sign-up using email,username and password.
2. How to login using email and password.
3. How to use Google for signup.
4.  How to use Google for signing in.
5. How change Profile image from the Avatar Dashboard by Clerk.
6. How change password, email, add or remove other contact information along with username from the Avatar Dashboard by Clerk.
7. How to Delete account from the Avatar Dashboard by Clerk.
8. How to check the personal git-hub stats from profile section after logging in.

author: koloml
body: Seems like Chromium avoids running the same script multiple times, even if this script is defined in multiple content script entries. But Firefox isn't doing that, causing AMD loader to throw an error about attempting to run the same module second time. This PR makes sure that module with the same name will be ignored if called more than once.

author: chrisrackauckas-claude
body:
## Summary

This PR comprehensively transforms FiniteDiff.jl documentation by adding detailed docstrings to all functions and completely restructuring the documentation organization for optimal usability.

### Comprehensive Documentation Added

**Main API Functions:**
- Enhanced `finite_difference_jacobian` with mathematical background and usage examples
- Complete `finite_difference_gradient` documentation covering both vector→scalar and scalar→vector cases
- Detailed `finite_difference_hessian` with mathematical formulation and complexity analysis
- Complete `finite_difference_jvp` documentation explaining Jacobian-vector products
- All corresponding in-place (`!`) versions with comprehensive usage notes

**Cache Constructors:**
- Full documentation for `JVPCache`, `GradientCache`, `HessianCache`, `DerivativeCache`
- Both allocating and non-allocating constructor variants documented
- Clear guidance on when to use each approach for optimal performance

**Internal Functions:**
- Complete documentation for epsilon computation functions (`compute_epsilon`)
- Detailed `default_relstep` with mathematical justification for step size choices
- Documentation for sparse Jacobian utilities (`_make_Ji`, `_colorediteration!`)
- Array utility functions (`_vec`, `_mat`, `setindex` overloads) with clear purpose statements

### Documentation Structure Reorganization

**New Page Organization:**
- **Home**: Package overview from README (clean, no API clutter)
- **Tutorials**: Existing tutorial content
- **Derivatives**: Single/multi-point scalar function derivatives
- **Gradients**: Vector→scalar and scalar→vector gradient computation
- **Jacobians**: Vector→vector functions with comprehensive sparse Jacobian guide
- **Hessians**: Scalar→matrix second derivatives with mathematical background
- **Jacobian-Vector Products**: Efficient directional derivatives without full Jacobians
- **Step Size Selection**: Mathematical theory and algorithms for optimal epsilon selection
- **Internal Utilities**: Complete coverage of internal functions for advanced users

**Improved Content Organization:**
- **Explanations first**: Each page provides context and theory before technical details
- **Logical flow**: Mathematical background → Performance notes → Function documentation
- **Focused content**: Each page concentrates on one functional area
- **Educational value**: Theory explanations help users understand when and how to use functions

### Documentation Features

**Mathematical Rigor:**
- Error analysis for truncation vs round-off errors
- Optimal step size derivations for each finite difference method
- Complexity analysis (e.g., "O(n) function evaluations, O(h²) accuracy")
- Mathematical formulations for Hessian approximations

**Practical Guidance:**
- Comprehensive parameter descriptions with types and purpose
- Usage examples with working code snippets
- Performance characteristics and trade-offs
- Cache management best practices
- Sparse Jacobian computation guidelines

**Professional Quality:**
- Consistent Julia docstring formatting
- Mathematical notation using LaTeX-style formatting
- Cross-references between related functions
- SciMLStyle code formatting applied throughout

## Technical Implementation

**Code Quality:**
- Applied JuliaFormatter with SciMLStyle to all modified files
- No breaking changes to existing API
- All existing tests continue to pass
- Added 40+ comprehensive docstrings following Julia conventions

**Documentation Build System:**
- Restructured `docs/pages.jl` for flat, intuitive navigation
- Updated `docs/make.jl` to generate clean index page from README
- Created 8 focused category pages replacing complex nested structure
- Documentation builds cleanly with proper cross-references

## Impact and Benefits

### For New Users
- **Accessible entry point**: Clear explanations of finite difference theory
- **Learning progression**: From basic concepts to advanced implementation details
- **Practical examples**: Working code snippets for all major functions
- **Method selection guidance**: When to use forward vs central vs complex step

### For Experienced Users
- **Complete reference**: Detailed parameter documentation for all functions
- **Performance optimization**: Complexity analysis and cache usage guidelines
- **Advanced features**: Sparse Jacobian computation and JVP efficiency
- **Internal understanding**: Documentation of algorithms and design decisions

### For Package Quality
- **Professional appearance**: Documentation quality now matches other top-tier Julia packages
- **Educational value**: Users learn finite difference theory alongside API usage
- **Maintainability**: Well-organized structure makes future updates easier
- **Accessibility**: Clear organization helps users find what they need quickly

## Before vs After

**Before**: Minimal docstrings like "Cache-less."
**After**: Comprehensive documentation with mathematical background, examples, performance analysis, and clear usage guidance.

This transformation makes FiniteDiff.jl significantly more accessible while preserving its performance-focused nature and adding educational value for users learning numerical differentiation.

author: cmb69
body:
Instead of using an inline script, we move the JavaScript into its own file.  Since the script uses some language strings, we put them into a data- attribute of the script element, so that we can easily access the information from JavaScript.   We also do that to signal whether the subscriber fields are mandatory.

Note that so far we do not cater to the many deficiencies of the existing JS (most notably that the script introduces several global variables which are not even "namespaced"), nor do we cater to efficiency (the script should either be written to `$bjs` or defered).

Note also that the script now requires a somewhat contemporary browser, while previously it was supposed to work even in ES3 environments (e.g. IE 6).  If that is a concern, the script could be adapted.

---

@olape-git, this should be sufficient to prevent the script from failing to execute with `script-src 'self'`. The more reasonable solution nowadays would likely be to use HTML5 form validation (what would allow to drop almost all of the JS, and would fix the limited email regexp).

* Open up [Helsinki lähelläsi page](https://helfi-etusivu.docker.so/fi/dev-etusivu/helsinki-lahellasi)

author: jlaitine
body:
## Summary

When delivering a signal to a kernel task, or any task in CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT with MMU enabled, the REG_SCTLR_EL1 needs to be stored for exception return.

Otherwise 0 is restored to the register at exception return, MMU is switched off and the  system crashes.

## Impact

Impacts arm64 signal delivery, fixes a system crash when signal is delivered to EL1 with MMU enabled.

## Testing

Tested on imx93 custom HW with 
- CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT: running in EL1, MMU enabled, SMP 2 cores, running "ostest"
- CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL

author: tristanpoland
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and new features to the Lighthouse autoscaling library, focusing on enhanced metrics persistence, configuration updates, and codebase cleanup. The most notable changes are the addition of metrics persistence and statistics capabilities, updates to project metadata, and removal of the Kubernetes example for streamlining.

**Metrics Persistence and Statistics (core feature additions):**
* Added `sqlx` and `statrs` as optional dependencies for metrics persistence and statistical analysis in `Cargo.toml`, along with new feature flags `metrics-persistence` and `predictive-scaling`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2e9d962a08321605940b5a657135052fbcef87b5e360662bb527c96d9a615542R45-R50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2e9d962a08321605940b5a657135052fbcef87b5e360662bb527c96d9a615542R89-R102)
* Introduced new engine commands (`GetHistoricalMetrics`, `GetMetricsStatistics`, `RunMaintenance`) and corresponding logic in `src/engine.rs` to support querying, statistics, and maintenance of historical metrics data when the `metrics-persistence` feature is enabled. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ff278ec599adfd033d35a083ebe8948db8bf177c9817dee8ddc4f3a9e3f5728eR35-R53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ff278ec599adfd033d35a083ebe8948db8bf177c9817dee8ddc4f3a9e3f5728eR240-R273)
* Added support for initializing the engine with a metrics store via `new_with_persistence` in `src/engine.rs`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ff278ec599adfd033d35a083ebe8948db8bf177c9817dee8ddc4f3a9e3f5728eR125-R158) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ff278ec599adfd033d35a083ebe8948db8bf177c9817dee8ddc4f3a9e3f5728eR102-R104)

**Project Metadata and Configuration (maintenance):**
* Updated author, homepage, and repository information in `Cargo.toml` to reflect new project ownership.
* Added a local settings file `.claude/settings.local.json` to define allowed shell commands for project automation and security.

**Examples and Documentation (streamlining):**
* Removed the `examples/kubernetes.rs` file, simplifying the codebase and focusing examples on core usage.
* Updated the `examples/basic_usage.rs` example to include the new `confidence` field in scaling thresholds, reflecting recent API changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-09f868950297c74c720a604834e21c00d8017c55f143c377988825408b0b7c8aR253-R261) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-09f868950297c74c720a604834e21c00d8017c55f143c377988825408b0b7c8aR375)
* Commented out the Kubernetes example configuration in `Cargo.toml` to match the removal of the example.

**Dependency Management (quality of life):**
* Added `rand` as a dependency for examples and ensured example dependencies are up to date.

These changes collectively improve the flexibility, maintainability, and feature set of the Lighthouse library, making it easier to use in production environments and to extend with new capabilities.

body:
When using 'manual_tax_amounts', both 'raw_tax_amount' & 'tax_amount' get the forced tax amount. However, by doing that, we lost accuracy in the raw amount. With this commit, the manual_tax_amounts become a way to ensure some results in '_round_base_lines_tax_details'. So after this commit, the manual_tax_amounts won't be manage in '_get_tax_details' anymore. That way, we could also use the manual_tax_amounts for amounts in company's currency.

For down payment/global discount, let's handle both currencies instead of only the foreign one. Also, the percentage is applied for each line to keep the whole thing as most accurate and close to the input percentage. If we don't do that, we could end up with a base of 99.99 and a tax amount of 15.01 for a tax of 15%.

Since the percentage is applied in a more "global" way, this commits also partially revert https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/3a269864534f234127c87ff1567f796904a27d5b

This approach is more complex and doesn't give always better results when using round_per_line either. Let's keep it simple and come back to a global approach.

author: nicolasdpr1
body:
Commit(s): Truncate json UUID before XML creation, remove index/offest and parent values from children keys

## What changes did you make?

In the saveICMdataHandler.js, the function saveICMdata has a point where the "data" from the form parameters is transformed into XML. Before this JSON -> XML change, I added a for-loop that goes through the key-pairs from "data" and creates a new JSON with keys that have their UUID truncated down to 8 characters. 
For children/dependants within the old JSON, they have their keys truncated from parent-offset-child, to just the child with an 8 character UUID.
Additionally, a wrapper value has been added around the parent-children lists.
Once the new JSON has been made, it is used to build the XML instead of the original JSON with the full UUIDs in the keys.

## Why did you make these changes?

As per https://dev.azure.com/BC-SDPR/Forms%20Modernization/_workitems/edit/3158, the ICM needs the XML values adjusted. With how long the UUIDs are, and especially with how long parent-offset-child could get, there was risk of going over the max character limit. Truncating the keys in a new JSON fixes this issue when the XML is created using the new, truncated keys paired with the old data values.

For the wrapper, this is to match ICM's standard practice of using the keyword "List" for lists (i.e. the parent-child sections). This wrapper can be added while parent-child values in the JSON are being updated, so no further updates would be needed once XML has been created.

## What alternatives did you consider?

I considered making these changes post-XML creation, however things would get very tricky while trying to add a wrapper and fix the parent-child tags. It was easier to do it all while creating a new JSON rather than tear apart and re-form the XML post its creation.

One risk that is not mitigated in this change is any duplication of the UUID's first 8 characters. This risk was deemed very minimal as we were assured we would never need to go XML -> JSON with full UUIDs.

- [ ] **My code meets the style guide**
- [ ] **My code has adequate test coverage (if applicable)**

author: kyrers
body:
This implements a custom modal for wallet connection.

**Note:** Unrelated to these changes, but the `swr` definition in `package.json` has been specified, because the project won't compile using the latest version.

<!-- start pr-codex -->

---

## PR-Codex overview
This PR focuses on enhancing the wallet connection experience, updating dependencies, and improving notification settings in the application. It introduces new features for wallet detection and connection, modifies service worker registration, and refines the user interface for better usability.

### Detailed summary
- Updated `swr` dependency version from `^2.2.0` to `2.2.0`.
- Added `handleAccountsChanged` function to handle account changes and reload the window if no accounts are present.
- Improved `subscribeUserToPush` function in `service-worker.js` for better promise handling.
- Modified `createDrizzle` function to accept a `customProvider`.
- Introduced `WalletConnector` component for wallet connection, including modal and error handling.
- Enhanced `Case` component with error handling for disputes and fallback to a 404 page.
- Improved wallet detection and connection logic in `wallet-connector.js`.
- Updated `NotificationSettings` component to streamline user settings management and improve user experience.
- Added styled components for better UI consistency in multiple components.

> ✨ Ask PR-Codex anything about this PR by commenting with `/codex {your question}`

<!-- end pr-codex -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Automatic wallet detection + optional auto‑connect to last used wallet; centered "Checking wallet…" spinner; wallet-required placeholder; "Connect Wallet" modal listing detected wallets with icons and connection flow.
  * Page reloads if wallet/account is cleared (accounts disconnected).

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Case page shows a 404 for invalid/inaccessible disputes.
  * More robust push-subscription flow with improved error handling.

* **Refactor**
  * Notification settings extracted into a dedicated component; notification UI modularized.

* **Chores**
  * Pinned swr dependency to exact 2.2.0.

body:
Added proofs showing that the type of natural numbers is isomorphic to it's own sum and product.

- Showed that if we have a function $f : \mathbb N \to \mathbb N$, which is increasing and starts at 0. We can then partition $\mathbb N$ into the pieces $[f k , f(k+1) )$. 
- Applying this fun fact to the double function, derived that $\mathbb N \cong \mathbb N + \mathbb N$
- Applying this fun fact to the function ($n \mapsto \frac{n (n+1)}{2} $), derived that $\mathbb N \cong \mathbb N \times \mathbb N$. 
- There are also some small lemmas on the order of natural numbers and increasing functions.

author: brandtnewton
body:
our parseTimestamp implementation used to support unix timestamps in seconds and microseconds, but it no longer does after [this commit](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-bigtable-ecosystem/commit/12b69b327f20b43ebb20fd9d87307640c4fcaf0b#diff-e21a9743d25761be4727486163b4085f1df134f2f95cc6e272843bb0a12e2f55) which neglected to remove the corresponding tests. 

I'm not sure why we supported non-millisecond timestamps, or how that wouldn't have broken low timestamp values, since it's impossible to infer a precision based on the number of digits. The Cassandra docs only list millisecond precision as being supported: https://docs.datastax.com/en/cql-oss/3.x/cql/cql_reference/timestamp_type_r.html

I also added some new tests for better coverage.

author: briankoco
body:
## Motivation

Tracing apparatus for KFD events was recently introduced. However, tracing is not currently enabled in rocprofv3, nor is tracing data dumped to the process' rocpd instance. This PR adds those features

## Technical Details

KFD/tracing updates:
- Add buffer_service_configs for each of the rocprofiler KFD buffer tracing types
- Introduce a new type `tool_buffer_tracing_kfd_record_t` which wraps the 7 different KFD buffer tracing types with an `std::variant` so that it's easier to pass data between the tool and output interfaces
- Add code to dump KFD records to rocpd. The format:
    - generate `rocpd_info_pmc` rows for each of the 7 main KFD event types
    - for each KFD event,
        - generate a `rocpd_event`, whose ID is used to associate the following table entries and whose `extdata` column encodes miscellaneous KFD data
        - generate a `rocpd_region` to track the process/agent info and the start/end timestamps
        - generate a `rocpd_pmc_event`, which tracks a derived value for each KFD event

A few bug fixes:
- KFD can report a special SVM location for prefetch locations. Look for those when processing prefetch locations in KFD records
    - e.g.: https://github.com/ROCm/amdgpu/blob/master/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdkfd/kfd_svm.c#L320
- KFD is supposed to pass the character '0' when  a successful queue restore is completed, and the character 'R' when the restore had to be rescheduled. A bug in the driver passed the NULL character '\0` instead of character '0', which is why successful queue restore events are parsed differently than restores (4 tokens instead of 5). This adds code to handle the proper reporting format, while also handling the broken format.

Output formats:
- The only output format supported by the tool is rocpd. However, support was also added to convert from rocpd to perfetto 

#### Proof of concept
To test drive, pass `--kfd-trace` to `rocprofv3`. You can then run the following queries on the SQL database to see how the data is being organized

```
SELECT
    rocpd_info_pmc.name AS kind,
    rocpd_string.string AS operation,
    rocpd_region.start, rocpd_region.end - rocpd_region.start as duration,
    rocpd_pmc_event.value, rocpd_event.extdata
FROM
    rocpd_event
JOIN rocpd_pmc_event    ON rocpd_pmc_event.event_id = rocpd_event.id
JOIN rocpd_region       ON rocpd_region.event_id    = rocpd_event.id
JOIN rocpd_string       ON rocpd_string.id          = rocpd_region.name_id
JOIN rocpd_info_pmc     ON rocpd_info_pmc.id        = rocpd_pmc_event.pmc_id
```

## Test Plan

Tests will be added and updated to accommodate kfd tracing data

## Test Result

The following tests were added:
- `tests/rocprofv3/kfd` - new test to validate format of JSON serialized KFD trace data

The following test/packages were updated:
- `tests/rocprofv3/tracing` - updated to validate KFD data when traced in concert with other tracers
- `tests/pytest-packages/tests/rocprofv3.py` - updated the logic used to validate JSON and CSV output formats when processing KFD trace data
- `tests/rocprofv3/negatte-aggregate-tracing-options` - extended with KFD flags

## Submission Checklist

- [x] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

author: jueshi
body:
This commit refactors the event handling logic for ticker selection and tab changes to be more robust and reliable.

Key changes:
- The `_on_ticker_selected` and `_on_watch_ticker_selected` methods now directly query the notebook widget to determine the active tab, rather than relying on a potentially stale instance variable (`self.active_tab`). This ensures that the correct view is updated when a ticker is selected.
- The `_compare_percentage_performance` method has been updated to accept an optional `tickers` argument, removing its dependency on a helper method that could cause unwanted side effects during the event loop.
- The `_on_tab_changed` handler was also updated to pass the selected tickers to the comparison method.

These changes fix a bug where the Fundamental Analysis tab would not update correctly and make the overall event handling logic more resilient.

author: stevedlawrence
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This is an alternate approach to PR #1504. I started adding assertions as suggested in that PR but many of them actually failed and couldn't be easily fixed. I realized that our logic to set elements as final was actually pretty broken and we just got lucky that things were mostly working. This required reworking the solution, but I think this is now easier to make sense of when things are marked as final and allows all the invariants to hold.

Our current logic to handle setting elements as final during parse is pretty broken. The core issue is that we primarily call setFinal in the sequence parser where it is difficult to know which elements are actually final--we had to make assumptions based on the results of the things actualy parsing elements. This usually worked, but in some cases could lead to setting an element final multiple times, or setting an element as final when it wasn't actually final.

A case where this flawed logic could lead to issues is with InfosetInputters that aren't designed to receive invalid infosets, such as JDOM or SAX inputters. Note that InfosetInputters aren't required to handle invalid infosets, except for those that are used by the debugger. This could lead to incomplete error diagnostics or misleading reasons for an error.

To make the final logic more clear and avoid these kinds of errors, DINode.isFinal is made private with new getFinal and setFinal method used instead. These functions allow us to place a number of assertions throughout the infoset logic to ensure we set things as final appropriately.

This also moves where we set elements as final. DISimple and DIComplex elements are set final in the ElementCombinatorParser and only when they successfully parse. This avoids cases where an element could be set final even though it failed to parse and removes any ambiguities about what sholud be set final. DIArrays are set final in the sequence parser that handles the ending of arrays, with special logic to handle arrays in unordered sequences. Note that the sequence parser is still responsible for attempting to walk the infoset to project the internal infoset into the target infoset--keeping all the walk logic in one place.

DAFFODIL-3006

## Problem

Users editing URLs directly in the browser or opening links from external apps would encounter JavaScript errors when the 404.html routing script executed:

```
SGEX route configuration not available - falling back to basic routing
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting 'innerHTML')
    at showErrorPage (smart-ips-pilgrimage:198:35)
```

## Root Cause

The 404.html contains JavaScript that executes immediately in the `<head>` section, before the `<body>` element exists. When an error occurs, `showErrorPage()` tries to set `document.body.innerHTML` but `document.body` is null because the DOM hasn't finished loading.

## Solution

This fix ensures the routing script waits for the DOM to be ready before executing and provides enhanced debugging information:

1. **DOM Ready Check**: Wrapped the main routing logic in a `performRouting()` function that only executes when the DOM is ready using `DOMContentLoaded` event listener
2. **Enhanced Error Handling**: Improved `showErrorPage()` to gracefully handle cases where `document.body` is not yet available with multiple fallback strategies
3. **Enhanced Route Configuration Logging**: Added detailed logging to show which configuration file was attempted and why it failed, including:
   - Which config file was attempted (routes-config.json vs routes-config.deploy.json)
   - Full URL that was attempted to be loaded
   - Deployment type detection results
   - Current path being processed
   - Specific reason for configuration failure
4. **Preserved Functionality**: All existing routing logic remains unchanged, only the timing of execution was fixed

## Technical Changes

- Added `DOMContentLoaded` event listener to ensure script waits for DOM
- Enhanced `showErrorPage()` with progressive fallback strategy:
  - Check if `document.body` exists
  - Wait for `DOMContentLoaded` if DOM is still loading
  - Use `setTimeout` as secondary fallback
  - Use `document.write` as last resort
- Enhanced `getRouteConfiguration()` to include comprehensive debugging information in console warnings

## Testing Results

- ✅ Error page now displays correctly without JavaScript errors
- ✅ Normal routing functionality preserved 
- ✅ Route configuration loading works properly
- ✅ Enhanced logging provides detailed debugging information for troubleshooting routing issues
- ✅ No regressions in existing functionality

![404 Error Page Working](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f9663c7-eef4-4f5a-9a37-b580c6988fe7)

The screenshot shows the 404 error page now displays correctly instead of throwing JavaScript errors, providing users with helpful links to return to the SGEX home page or report bugs.

Fixes #794.

## Summary

- **Enhanced `stn template create` command** with new `--env` flag for creating bundles from existing environments
- **Comprehensive environment scanning** that automatically detects MCP configs, agent prompts, and template variables
- **Proper Go template parsing** replaces fragile regex-based variable extraction for robust template compatibility
- **Complete bundle structure generation** with manifest, agents, examples, and JSON schema

## Key Features

### 🎯 **Enhanced CLI Usage**
```bash
# Create bundle from existing environment
stn template create my-bundle --env default --name "My Bundle" --author "Dev Team"

# Original empty bundle creation still works  
stn template create empty-bundle --name "Starter Bundle"
```

### 🔍 **Intelligent Environment Scanning**
- **MCP Configurations**: Auto-detects and merges all `.json` MCP config files
- **Agent Prompts**: Scans `.prompt` files with full dotprompt frontmatter support
- **Template Variables**: Extracts variables like `{{ .ROOT_PATH }}` with proper Go template parsing

### 🛡️ **Robust Variable Extraction**
- **No more fragile regex\!** Uses Go's `text/template.Parse()` + AST walking
- **Handles complex templates**: Supports spacing, functions, conditionals, ranges
- **Production-ready**: Same template engine used throughout Station codebase

### 📦 **Enhanced Bundle Structure**
- **manifest.json**: Rich metadata with variable schema, agent listings, source environment
- **template.json**: Merged MCP server configurations with conflict resolution
- **agents/**: All agent prompt files with preserved dotprompt frontmatter
- **examples/**: `development.vars.yml` with actual variable values for easy deployment
- **variables.schema.json**: JSON Schema for proper bundle validation

## Test Plan

- [x] **Build and compilation**: All code builds successfully with proper imports
- [x] **Bundle creation**: `stn template create test-bundle --env default` works perfectly
- [x] **Environment scanning**: Correctly scans 2 MCP configs, 12 agents, 1 variable
- [x] **Template parsing**: Proper Go template variable extraction (no regex)
- [x] **Bundle validation**: `stn template validate` passes with proper metadata
- [x] **Bundle packaging**: `stn template bundle` creates distributable `.tar.gz`
- [x] **End-to-end installation**: `stn template install` deploys all components correctly
- [x] **Backward compatibility**: Original empty bundle creation unchanged

## Technical Implementation

### Variable Extraction Improvements
**Before (Fragile):**
```go
// BAD: Regex breaks with spacing, functions, conditionals
templateVarRegex := regexp.MustCompile(`\{\{\s*\.\s*([A-Z_]+[A-Z0-9_]*)\s*\}\}`)
```

**After (Robust):**
```go
// GOOD: Uses Go's actual template parser + AST traversal
tmpl, err := template.New("scan").Parse(content)
visitor := &templateVariableVisitor{variables: variableSet}
visitor.visitNode(tmpl.Tree.Root)
```

### Enhanced Bundle Creation Workflow
1. **Environment Detection**: Validates environment exists and is accessible
2. **MCP Config Scanning**: Walks directory tree, detects `.json` files with `mcpServers`
3. **Agent Prompt Scanning**: Processes `.prompt` files with dotprompt frontmatter
4. **Variable Analysis**: Uses Go template parser to extract all variable references
5. **Bundle Structure Creation**: Generates complete bundle with metadata and examples
6. **Validation Ready**: Creates bundles that pass `stn template validate`

This enables the seamless workflow requested: **"stn template create --env default and it creates a bundle out of the existing mcp servers, agents, and variable keys"** while excluding actual variable values but including them in the manifest schema.

## Summary
- Fixed existing halving/movement bugs for consistency
- Added comprehensive window organization features
- Implemented persistent, resolution-independent layouts

## Bug Fixes
- ✅ Fixed `left-half`/`right-half` to use actual 50% widths (were using undefined widths)
- ✅ Fixed `moveWindowRight` to match `moveWindowLeft` behavior (was resizing instead of just moving)
- ✅ Consolidated Y-coordinate flipping in `setWindowFrame` (removed skipYFlipping parameter)
- ✅ Fixed CI workflow to generate missing `mwm.sha256` file
- ✅ Added `--version` command support

## New Features

### Window Organization
- `arrange grid <COLS>x<ROWS> [gap-<px>]` - Tile all windows on current screen
- `arrange cascade [offset-<px>]` - Fan out windows with fixed offset
- `arrange columns <N> [gap-<px>]` - Equal-width vertical slices
- `arrange rows <N> [gap-<px>]` - Equal-height horizontal slices

### Layout Management
- `layout save <name>` - Capture current screen's window layout (relative percentages)
- `layout restore <name>` - Restore positions/sizes, resilient to resolution changes

### Enhanced Snapping
- `snap-up` - Snap to nearest window above
- `snap-down` - Snap to nearest window below

### Fine Control
- `nudge <left|right|up|down> <px>` - Move by pixels without resizing
- `grow <width|height> <±px>` - Resize by edge

### Display & Information
- `display-under-mouse` - Move window to display under cursor
- `list-windows [--json]` - List all visible windows with optional JSON output

## Test Plan
- [x] Build project with `swift build`
- [ ] Test half commands produce actual 50% widths
- [ ] Test move commands preserve window size
- [ ] Test arrange grid/cascade/columns/rows commands
- [ ] Test layout save/restore across resolution changes

- [ ] Test nudge/grow pixel-perfect control
- [ ] Test display-under-mouse with multiple monitors
- [ ] Test list-windows JSON output
- [ ] Verify CI produces mwm.sha256 on release

author: tsutomi
body:
This pull request introduces a new authentication mechanism for messaging connectors, adds Firebase connector projects to the solution, and improves the handling of HTML content parts. The main focus is on extensible authentication support, including new abstractions, providers, and integration patterns. Additionally, dependencies are updated and solution/project configuration is expanded.

**Authentication Mechanism Implementation:**

* Added comprehensive documentation describing the new authentication mechanism, including abstractions (`IAuthenticationProvider`, `AuthenticationCredential`, etc.), built-in providers (API Key, OAuth2 Client Credentials, Firebase), and integration patterns for connectors.
* Introduced the `AuthenticationCredential` class, which encapsulates credential details (type, value, expiration, properties), and provides factory methods for creating token, API key, and basic credentials.

**Solution/Project Configuration:**

* Added new projects for Firebase connector and its unit tests to the solution file (`Deveel.Messaging.Connector.Firebase`, `Deveel.Messaging.Connector.Firebase.XUnit`).
* Updated solution configuration to include build and platform settings for the new Firebase projects. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d12b4991fdf0d562c041ce3dc14e9790845713a061ebe4402f0d61271bd2aec5R170-R193) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d12b4991fdf0d562c041ce3dc14e9790845713a061ebe4402f0d61271bd2aec5R209-R210)
* Added conditional package references for `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` targeting .NET 8.0 and 9.0 in the connector abstractions project.

**Messaging Improvements:**

* Improved the `HtmlContentPart` constructor to default the `Html` property to an empty string if null, preventing potential null reference issues.

author: ramanshrivastava
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: cidrblock
body:
## Problem
When `ansible-lint` runs on collections for the first time, it fails to discover plugins from collections installed by `ansible-compat` during `prepare_environment()`. The issue occurs because Ansible's plugin loader is initialized too early with incomplete collection paths, before `prepare_environment()` has a chance to install dependencies.

## Root Cause
The plugin loader was being initialized during `Runtime.__init__()` or early module imports, capturing collection paths before:
1. Collections are installed from `requirements.yml` and `galaxy.yml` dependencies
2. The cache directory (`/.ansible/collections`) is populated
3. `ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH` includes the newly installed collections

The problem was particularly acute because `ansible-lint`'s `Templar` class internally uses Ansible's collection loader for template rendering and plugin discovery. When the plugin loader was initialized early with incomplete paths, `Templar` would fail to find collections that were installed during `prepare_environment()`, leading to template rendering failures and missing plugin errors.

## Solution
Introduced a **plugin loader gate** mechanism to delay initialization until the environment is fully prepared:

### 1. Gated Plugin Loader Access
- Added `Runtime.plugin_loader_enabled` class variable (defaults to `False`)
- Modified `Plugins.__getattribute__` to raise `RuntimeError` if plugin loader is accessed before being enabled
- This provides clear error messages when the loader is accessed prematurely

### 2. Explicit Plugin Loader Enablement  
- Added `Runtime.enable_plugin_loader()` method to explicitly initialize the plugin loader
- Moved plugin loader initialization from `_ensure_module_available()` to this dedicated method
- `ansible-lint` now calls `enable_plugin_loader()` after `prepare_environment()` completes

### 3. Enhanced State Management
- Modified `Runtime.clean()` to reset both `initialized` and `plugin_loader_enabled` flags
- Added module unloading for `ansible.plugins.*`, `ansible.utils.collection_loader`, and `ansible.collections.*` to ensure fresh state between test runs

## Changes Made
- **runtime.py**: Added plugin loader gating and explicit enablement
- **test_runtime.py**: Added test for plugin loader gating behavior

## Impact
- First-run collection discovery now works reliably
- Plugin loader initialization is deterministic and controlled  
- Templar can access collections installed during prepare_environment through the properly initialized collection loader
- Better error messages when plugin loader is accessed prematurely
- Improved test isolation through enhanced state cleanup
- No breaking changes to existing `ansible-compat` API

This change ensures that `ansible-lint` can successfully discover and use collection plugins on the first run, eliminating the "works on second run" behavior that users were experiencing.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This refactoring changes the `parseValue` method in all item types to accept the `editControl` directly, rather than the entire form. 

The main benefits of this change are:
- The `parseValue` methods are now simpler, as they no longer need to query the form to find the relevant input.
- This change improves the separation of concerns, as the `parseValue` methods are no longer dependent on the form's structure.

The following files were updated:
- `src/components/item-form.js`: The call to `parseValue` was updated to pass the `editControl` instead of the `form`.
- `src/types/BooleanType.js`: The `parseValue` method was updated to accept the `editControl` and return its `checked` property.
- `src/types/ListType.js`: The `parseValue` method was updated to accept the `editControl` for consistency, although it is not used.
- `src/types/NumberType.js`: The `parseValue` method was updated to accept the `editControl` and return its numeric value.
- `src/types/TextType.js`: The `parseValue` method was updated to accept the `editControl` and return its value.

body:
## Summary
  Adds a new data export feature to the PocketBase admin UI, allowing users
   to export collection records as JSON files directly from the collections
   interface.

  ## Features
  - **Export button** in collections header (next to settings and refresh)
  - **Field selection** with checkboxes to choose which fields to export
  - **Scope options**: Export all records or current filtered results
  - **Real-time preview** showing first 3 records with selected fields
  - **Smart validation**: Prevents exporting when no records match filter
  - **Consistent UI**: Uses existing PocketBase components and design
  patterns

  ## Implementation Details
  - New `ExportDataPanel.svelte` component using existing `OverlayPanel`
  - Integrates with current authentication (superuser permissions)
  - Follows PocketBase naming conventions and UI patterns
  - Excludes hidden fields from export options
  - Generates descriptive filenames:
  `{collection}_{scope}_{timestamp}.json`

  ## UI/UX
  - Slide-in panel matching existing "New record" and "API Preview"
  interfaces
  - Loading states and proper error handling
  - Visual feedback for empty results and field selection
  - Tooltip support and accessibility features

  ## Testing
  - Tested with various collections and field types
  - Validated with filtered and unfiltered record sets
  - Confirmed proper handling of empty results and hidden fields

author: santiagovillane
body:
## 📄 Description
This PR implements the `RandomPolicy` class, which extends the `PolicyInterface` and defines a Petri net transition selection policy based on random choice.

The policy receives an array representing the indices of currently enabled transitions and randomly selects one, ensuring that all enabled transitions have equal priority.

---

## 🛠 Implementation Details
- Added a `private final Random random` field to maintain a single `Random` instance for the lifetime of the policy, avoiding unnecessary object creation.
- Implemented the `choose(int[] n)` method:
  - ✅ Validates that the array is **not null** or **empty**.
  - 🎲 Uses `random.nextInt(n.length)` to select a random index.
  - 🔄 Returns the corresponding transition index from the array.
- The policy remains **independent** of the internal Petri net structure; it operates only on the set of enabled transitions provided as input.

---

## Summary
- Moved filtering logic from `cmd/tdh/list.go` to `pkg/tdh/commands.go` to maintain clean architecture
- Added `ShowDone` and `ShowAll` fields to `ListOptions` struct for filtering control
- Updated `List` function in pkg layer to handle filtering based on options

## Changes
- **cmd/tdh/list.go**: Removed filtering logic, now passes flags directly to pkg API
- **pkg/tdh/commands.go**: Enhanced `ListOptions` struct and `List` function to handle filtering
- Removed unnecessary `models` import from cmd layer

## Architecture Benefits
This change ensures the cmd layer only handles CLI parsing, validation, and output formatting, while all business logic remains in the pkg layer. This follows the project's strict cmd/pkg architecture pattern.

## Test Results
- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ Linting clean (golangci-lint)
- ✅ Manual testing confirms filtering works correctly:
  - `tdh list` - shows only pending todos
  - `tdh list --done` - shows only completed todos
  - `tdh list --all` - shows all todos

Closes #5

body:
### Ticket
[Link to Github Issue
](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/issues/26627)

### Problem description
We need to provide an operation to TT-train that allows then to create a tensor from a memory array (like pytorch does with from_buffer)

### What's changed
Created a new operation that based on the data type we are trying to fill, it will generate a tensor with the data provided, similarly to pytorch. The only difference is that our tensors are immutable, so changing the data in the tensor won't affect the data in the array.
Also given that python is less strict with types, I had to handle bfloat in python and create an array of data based on the type requested in the operation instead of deducing it from the vector. This is also a limitation in pytorch

author: smellslikeml
body:
This experiment integrates uncertainty quantification into the data synthesis pipeline, inspired by the core ideas of the VQASynth project. While VQASynth currently generates point estimates for spatial properties like 3D coordinates, this feature introduces a method to produce calibrated prediction sets, which provide a statistically rigorous measure of confidence for each prediction.

We draw from the SOURCE repository, `ElSacho/Gaussian_Conformal_Prediction`, which implements a method to create prediction sets for multivariate regression tasks. The method, 'Gaussian Conformal Prediction', models uncertainty as a Gaussian distribution and uses a calibration set to ensure that for a given confidence level (e.g., 90%), the true outcome is contained within the predicted set with that frequency. This is ideal for VQASynth's goal of generating high-quality spatial data, as it allows us to quantify the reliability of the generated 3D locations.

This branch adds a minimal, self-contained proof-of-concept in `experiments/conformal-prediction/run.py`. The script simulates predicting 3D coordinates from abstract image embeddings and applies the conformal prediction workflow. It trains a model to predict not just the coordinates (mean), but also an uncertainty ellipsoid (covariance matrix) around them. This demonstrates a practical path to enhancing the VQASynth dataset with valuable uncertainty information, making the synthetic data more robust for training downstream models.


### Test Strategy
- Ensure a Python environment with `torch`, `numpy`, and `tqdm` is available. A CUDA-enabled environment is recommended for performance.
- Navigate to the root of the repository.
- Execute the experiment script via the command line: `python experiments/conformal-prediction/run.py`.
- Observe the script's output, checking for the final results table.


### Success Criteria
- The script runs to completion without any errors.
- The final 'Actual coverage' printed to the console should be approximately equal to the 'Target coverage' of 0.90 (e.g., within the range [0.85, 0.95]).
- The script successfully calculates and prints a non-zero 'Average prediction set volume', demonstrating that the uncertainty model is generating valid outputs.


**Labels:** data-synthesis, uncertainty-quantification

---
**Source:** https://github.com/ElSacho/Gaussian_Conformal_Prediction
**Evidence:**
- `README.md`
- `code/gaussian_predictor_levelsets.py`
- `code/network.py`
- `code/example_of_usage.ipynb`

body:
This PR implements a complete Google Apps Script backend solution for processing client intake form submissions with support for multiple service selections and automatic fee calculation.

## What's Added

### Google Apps Script Backend (`Code.gs`)
- Complete form processing logic that handles multiple service selections
- Automatic fee calculation based on predefined service pricing
- Google Spreadsheet integration with structured data storage
- Email confirmation system for client notifications
- Robust error handling and validation
- Support for the required field format (`Service Requested[]` array)

### Updated Intake Forms
Both `intake.html` and `intake-form.html` have been enhanced with:
- **Service selection interface** supporting the required services:
  - Standard Consulting Fee ($100)
  - CPA Referral Coordination ($150) 
  - Bookkeeping Referral Coordination ($120)
  - Grant Submission ($200)
  - Business Plan Writing ($250)
  - Nonprofit Formation ($300)
- **Visual pricing display** so clients can see costs upfront
- **Multiple service selection** with proper field naming for backend compatibility
- **Real-time fee calculation** and confirmation dialogs
- **Form validation** ensuring required fields are completed
- **Responsive design** that works across devices

### Spreadsheet Integration
The backend creates a structured spreadsheet with:
- Individual Yes/No columns for each service (visible in spreadsheet only)
- Total fee calculation column
- Complete client information capture
- Services summary for easy review
- Timestamp tracking for submissions

### Documentation
Comprehensive `README.md` with:
- Complete setup instructions for Google Apps Script deployment
- Service pricing reference
- Form field structure documentation
- Troubleshooting guide
- Customization instructions

## Key Features

- **Multiple Service Support**: Clients can select multiple services simultaneously
- **Automatic Fee Calculation**: Total fees are calculated and displayed in real-time
- **Backend Integration**: Ready for Google Apps Script deployment with minimal configuration
- **Data Structure**: Spreadsheet columns match requirements (Yes/No per service, subtotal visible to admin only)
- **Client Experience**: Clean, professional forms with clear pricing transparency
- **Admin Dashboard**: Structured spreadsheet data for easy management and reporting

## Usage

1. Deploy the `Code.gs` script as a Google Apps Script web app
2. Update the form action URLs to point to the deployed script
3. Configure the spreadsheet ID in the script
4. Forms are ready to accept submissions with automatic processing

The implementation fully addresses the requirements for supporting multiple service selections, calculating total fees, and providing the necessary spreadsheet structure for business operations.

author: sierra-moxon
body:
- added parallel processing (and `max-workers`, default 10, 20 works better, and `batch-size` default 100 params to cli) & progress reporting.  Also added some code to help Ctrl-C out of the script with w/threading in mind. 
   - removed index step that was calling go.db on every model translation (very slow).  minerva_wrapper already handles the ontology walking.
   - pre-build/cache some of the URI expansion and name lookup calls
- added check to only dump models that have edges, this still pulls in nodes that may not be connected, but are in the same model as we do currently.  But models with no edges at all are blocked from being dumped. 
- moved some logger.warnings to logger.debug to streamline output.

A slight tangent to the named fixes in this PR is a small addition to the cx2 translation that, when run as part of the translate-collection cli, will follow the logic of the networkx translation and only spit out models that have at least one molecular activity with one `causal_association` member.  This eliminates models like this on: [586fc17a00000528](http://noctua.geneontology.org/workbench/noctua-alliance-pathway-preview/?model_id=gomodel:586fc17a00000528) that have relationships between BP and MF terms and are identified by our SPARQL mechanism as "causal".  There are about 290 of these.  

However, the `causal_association` logic in this code base is also in some ways _more_ permissive of "causality" than what is currently produced by the SPARQL.  For details, see [this slide](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Te9fZZqTqYGisEdjyGbTJy-zhhJzyTi-NOxn0LWlxk8/edit?slide=id.g374f7f428aa_0_0#slide=id.g374f7f428aa_0_0).  And so, this method `translate-collection` actually produces _more_ causal models for NDex (cx2 format) than before. 

If NDex output needs to be generated separately, without this requirement added, it can still be called (by not using the translate-collection cli), but we want to start using this Python logic in the future.

author: ryanjjung
body:
## Description of the Change

Per Issue #147, we would like to have a way of granting a person access to an application environment's resources without those permissions spilling over into other environments. We want to be able to grant admin access to an env when it's necessary (like giving a developer access to a personal testing environment or granting a CI user the ability to manipulate its own environment), and read-only access at other times (f/ex, giving a security auditor the ability to inspect infrastructure without manipulating it). To accomplish this, we make two main changes here.

First, I refactored the code that gives us access to a stack's resources in its fully applied state so that it no longer lives in the monitoring code, but instead now has a home at the base of the tb_pulumi module. This is a `ProjectResourceGroup`. You can now easily create these "post-apply" features by simply extending this class and implementing its `ready` function. The `monitoring.MonitoringGroup` class is now such an extension, but is otherwise unchanged here.

Second, I added a new `ProjectResourceGroup` called `StackAccessPolicies`. This creates IAM policies for each service that you have resources in. One of these offers read-only access to only the resources in this singular stack (read: "environment"), the other full admin access. The commentary in the code contains a lot of details I won't repeat here as to why this is the best model for us, but suffice it to say that there are some complexities to work around here.

## Benefits

We can now stick users in these user groups (or even attach these policies directly) to better control access within an environment.

## Applicable Issues

#147

author: smellslikeml
body:
This experiment integrates the `ExperimentLogger` from the `causal-reasoning-in-pieces` (SOURCE) repository into VQASynth (TARGET). The SOURCE repo demonstrates a highly modular architecture for complex reasoning tasks, and its components, like the logger, are well-designed for reusability and robust experiment tracking. The logger creates a timestamped and job-ID-labeled CSV file, automatically handles headers, and provides methods for appending single or multiple records, which is a significant improvement over ad-hoc print statements or manual file handling.

By incorporating this utility into the VQASynth pipeline, we can introduce a more structured and standardized way to log the outputs of the data generation stages. This is particularly useful for tracking the large volume of VQA pairs, metadata, and reasoning chains produced. A standardized CSV output facilitates easier analysis, debugging, and comparison between different data generation runs.

This feature branch introduces the logger and a simple demonstration script within a new `experiments/` directory. The demo simulates the generation of VQA data and logs it to a CSV file, showcasing how this component can be adopted within the broader VQASynth data synthesis pipeline to improve reproducibility and data management.


### Test Strategy
- Set up a Python virtual environment and install dependencies from the target repo's `requirements.txt`.
- Run the demonstration script from the root of the repository: `python experiments/logging_demo/run.py`.
- Verify that the `output/logging_demo/` directory is created.
- Inspect the generated CSV file inside the output directory. Its name should match the pattern `experiment_results_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_ffffff_vqa-gen-xxxxxxxx.csv`.
- Open the CSV file and confirm that it contains a header row and 6 data rows with the correct content generated by the script.


### Success Criteria
- The script `experiments/logging_demo/run.py` executes without errors.
- A structured CSV log file is created in the `output/logging_demo` directory.
- The CSV file contains headers that match the keys of the dictionaries being logged.
- The rows in the CSV file accurately reflect the data generated in the demonstration script.


**Labels:** experiment, data-synthesis

---
**Source:** https://github.com/kacperkadziolka/causal-reasoning-in-pieces

- `causal_discovery/experiment_logger.py`

author: skolem
body:
[Shortcut 9750](https://app.shortcut.com/rinsed/story/9750) - This adds support for lookup of Canadian cities and provinces by the first three characters of a Canadian postal code. Using only the first three characters makes the Canadian zipcode database a reasonable size. Using all six characters, which encode location down to the street, would be 50 Meg or more. We only need to determine the city and province to support Sonnys operations so the first three characters are enough.

Details on Canadian postal code format is here: https://www.canadapost-postescanada.ca/cpc/en/support/articles/addressing-guidelines/postal-codes.page

Scripts and more documentation were added so we can more easily rebuild the US and Canadian zipcode CSV files. The original source files for the generated CSVs were also added to the repo in case they go away from their online locations.

author: acemavrick
body:
This pull request introduces basic, anonymous analytics to the application, allowing the collection of functional usage data to help improve the app and understand feature usage patterns. Analytics are enabled by default but can be disabled by the user. The implementation includes backend event logging, updates to the user interface to inform users about analytics, and refactoring to support configuration and analytics initialization. Additionally, the build configuration is simplified for easier maintenance.

**Analytics Implementation**

* Added a new `webapp/analytics.py` module to handle analytics event logging, session management, and device information collection, with opt-out capability via the application support directory.
* Integrated analytics event logging into key backend actions in `webapp/app.py`, including downloads, cache operations, info refreshes, shutdown, and path changes, ensuring events are sent and errors are handled gracefully. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54L21-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R331-R342) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R391-R400) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R469) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R486) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R619-R621) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R850-R859) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54R999-R1001)
* Added an `analytics_enabled` flag to the index route and template to inform users when analytics are active, with a corresponding notice and link to the README. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-55f12a9f17b4ba61d3e37852150b7d78b8aedbe3629bc4ce8173d4b572297a54L285-R310) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3b4f502e270c074cd1eafffb45bc0628ce5b9f9920588a8f8500e064d8af4851R185-R190)

**Documentation**

* Updated `README.md` with a new Analytics section explaining what data is collected, how it is processed, and how users can disable analytics. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R105-R110)

**Configuration and Refactoring**

* Moved the app data directory logic to a new `config.py` for cleaner initialization and usage across the codebase. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-117426151e93a626f8b46bfdb3a95b3f4a62e5f4dd6e65975a7c50759bf04482R1-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b10564ab7d2c520cdd0243874879fb0a782862c3c902ab535faabe57d5a505e1L8-L17) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b10564ab7d2c520cdd0243874879fb0a782862c3c902ab535faabe57d5a505e1R212-R214)

**Build Configuration Simplification**

* Simplified `main.spec` by removing dynamic version and metadata extraction, hardcoding bundle identifiers and version fields for easier maintenance and reliability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3eb226cc2f2bc2a5f8a541cd708d5f9299d392918dc5562f71ac194f87b9d35fL2-L24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3eb226cc2f2bc2a5f8a541cd708d5f9299d392918dc5562f71ac194f87b9d35fL77-R54) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-3eb226cc2f2bc2a5f8a541cd708d5f9299d392918dc5562f71ac194f87b9d35fL92-R76)
